correctness.rationale: PASS: The actual proof transfers the Hausdorff coefficient action to the affine semigroup T(t)f(z)=f(1-e^-t+e^-t z) on H^1 and D^1. The norm estimate ||T(t)||<=C e^t and a commuting binomial expansion bound the spectral radius by R=ae^u+be^v. The exact identity T(t)(1-z)^(-s)=e^(ts)(1-z)^(-s) holds, with analytic powers in both preduals when Re s<1. For an arbitrary nonzero |lambda|<R, a real x<1 and two non-collinear phases yield a simple zero of G_x(theta1,theta2)=ae^(ux+i theta1)+be^(vx+i theta2)-lambda. Because u/v is irrational, the one-parameter phase orbit (u t,v t) is dense on the torus; phase returns approximate the chosen simple zero. Rouché on a small complex disk wholly within Re s<1 produces distinct actual roots s_j, not merely approximate spectral values. The corresponding (1-z)^(-s_j) are linearly independent eigenvectors, making lambda I-A non-Fredholm on each predual. Fredholm essential spectra are closed, so zero and the circle are included; duality yields the same two spectral disks on BMOA and Bloch. This is an analytic argument without a finite computational premise. Mathematical boundary: irrationality and strictly positive atomic masses are essential.
